sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 1! On Canvas 1, explore the 7-node W3C PROV-O pipeline multigraph connecting raw data, cleaning, tokens, training, and models. On Canvas 2, toggle between Upstream Ancestry and Downstream Blast Radius to compute reachability cones dynamically.
Dr. Nova, let's test the causal reachability engine! When CleanTokens is tainted, watch the blast radius isolate downstream training and weights, while upstream raw sensors remain untouched!

Active Checkpoint 1! Curators discover an annotator label inversion error in HumanLabels across a multi-stage NLP pipeline. Compute the downstream blast radius of HumanLabels, and determine whether RawWiki text is affected.
Active Checkpoint 1 challenge! If human labels are corrupted, what is the exact downstream blast radius, and does it require re-extracting raw Wikipedia text?

Masterclass derivation! Option B is correct. The downstream blast radius contains TrainClassifier, ModelV1, Evaluate, and MetricsJSON. Because RawWiki is an upstream ancestor rather than a descendant in the DAG, it is completely unaffected and does not need to be re-extracted!

Incorrect. Option B is correct. In a directed acyclic graph, influence flows strictly downstream. HumanLabels affects only the downstream classifier, model weights, and evaluation metrics. RawWiki and extracted vectors are upstream ancestors, completely outside the blast radius.

Welcome to Interactive Lab 2! On Canvas 1, simulate quality attenuation across twelve pipeline stages and toggle active quality gates to arrest decay. On Canvas 2, inspect the Gantt timeline and inject look-ahead leakage to observe the temporal logic linter in action.
Dr. Nova, look at the temporal timeline! Injecting look-ahead leakage immediately triggers a red conflict line because training starts before input signal generation completes!

Active Checkpoint 2! Consider a two-step pipeline starting with initial quality zero point nine five. Stage one has fidelity zero point nine zero and noise zero point zero two. Stage two has fidelity zero point eight five and noise zero point zero five. Calculate the terminal quality under Theorem 13.5.1.
Active Checkpoint 2! Calculate the two-stage quality decay under Theorem 13.5.1. What is the terminal quality, and what percentage of data fidelity was lost?

Outstanding calculation! Option A is correct. Stage one yields zero point eight three five. Stage two scales by zero point eight five and subtracts zero point zero five, yielding zero point six six zero! This represents a thirty point five percent loss in data fidelity across just two transformations.

That's not right. Option A is correct. Applying Theorem 13.5.1: Q1 equals zero point nine零 times zero point nine five minus zero point zero two, which is zero point eight three five. Q2 equals zero point eight five times zero point eight three five minus zero point zero five, yielding zero point six six zero.

Active Checkpoint 3! An automated pipeline log records Entity_FilteredSignals generated at t equals 180, while Activity_TrainNeuralNet starts at t equals 150 and uses FilteredSignals. Identify the formal constraint violated and the machine learning pathology it represents.
Final checkpoint! Why is an activity starting at t equals 150 and using an entity generated at t equals 180 a fatal bug, and what is the modeling pathology?

Brilliant diagnosis! Option C is correct. The log violates the Generation-Usage Ordering constraint, which mandates that generation time must be less than or equal to activity start time. In machine learning, this represents look-ahead data leakage where future signals contaminate training, producing bogus offline benchmark scores!

Incorrect. Option C is correct. Generation timestamp 180 is strictly greater than start timestamp 150, violating the Generation-Usage Ordering constraint. This temporal paradox indicates look-ahead bias and data leakage, where future information contaminates training.
